facts.statement: Under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication (SCA), an electronic payment must be authenticated with at least two independent factors drawn from knowledge, possession, and inherence; a single SMS one-time code alone does not satisfy SCA because it is not dynamically linked to the transaction.
facts.source_title: Open Banking, PSD2, & Strong Customer Authentication

facts.statement: Authentication codes generated for a payment must be dynamically linked to that specific transaction's amount and payee, so a captured code cannot be replayed against a different transaction.

The mobile app should run within a shielded, isolated execution environment resistant to overlay attacks, code injection, and keylogging, since PSD2's Regulatory Technical Standards call for a separated secure execution environment for mobile payment actions.

New-customer onboarding must include a Customer Identification Program that verifies government ID and identity details, and the bank must perform ongoing Customer Due Diligence on existing accounts, per Bank Secrecy Act / anti-money-laundering requirements.

Any component that stores, processes, or transmits card data must comply with PCI DSS v4.0.1: no storage of full card numbers or CVV, and strong access controls and logging for any system handling cardholder data.
facts.source_title: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Sets New Baseline For Cardholder Data Security

facts.statement: The bank must run an ongoing anti-money-laundering monitoring program capable of flagging suspicious transaction patterns (unusual amounts, velocity, or destinations) for manual review and, where required, regulatory reporting.
facts.source_title: 5 essential steps for KYC/AML onboarding and compliance
